dimensions.label: Problem Clarity
dimensions.evidence: The electron-authkit-example repo hand-wires the full AuthKit OAuth/session lifecycle across src/main/auth, src/preload, and src/renderer, demonstrating the boilerplate and latent bugs every integrator currently re-derives.

dimensions.label: Goal Definition
dimensions.evidence: Goals are observable outcomes: one call per Electron context, zero re-implemented crypto via the core, public-client (no API key), refresh-token confinement, secure at-rest persistence, and lockstep-versioned ESM subpath exports.

dimensions.label: Success Criteria
dimensions.evidence: Each goal maps to a runnable check — coverage-gated vitest, a crypto-delegation grep guard, per-ceremony-mode Playwright e2e, ESM export resolution, build/typecheck, and lint — all exit-0 gated.

dimensions.label: Scope Boundaries
dimensions.evidence: Explicit in/out/future lists: native passkeys and non-React bindings are out with rationale; public-client config, both ceremony modes, and the example app are in.

dimensions.label: Consistency
dimensions.evidence: No contradictions remain; storage-seam divergence, session-via-safeStorage, public-client (no API key, bypassing getWorkOS), and ESM-only output all carry stated rationale.

problem: WorkOS AuthKit has no Electron SDK. Integrating it today means hand-wiring the full OAuth and session lifecycle across Electron's three isolated process contexts — main, preload, and renderer — as the electron-authkit-example repo does across src/main/auth/ (auth.ts, deep-link-handler.ts, ipc-handlers.ts), src/preload/index.ts, and the renderer's src/renderer/src/hooks/useAuth.ts.

That hand-wiring concentrates several error-prone, security-sensitive concerns in application code: PKCE generation and expiry, authorization-code exchange, JWT-exp parsing and token refresh, the cross-platform custom-protocol deep-link capture matrix (open-url on macOS, second-instance on Windows/Linux, the dev-mode argv branch), safeStorage-backed persistence behind a hardcoded key, and a private IPC contract whose channel names are duplicated between preload and main behind a fragile 'must match' comment. The renderer additionally redefines its own User type (useAuth.ts), which drifts from @workos-inc/node's.

Every team adopting AuthKit on Electron re-derives this same boilerplate and inherits the same latent bugs. WorkOS already ships @workos/authkit-session — the framework-agnostic core powering @workos/authkit-tanstack-react-start — whose AuthKitCore and AuthOperations are cookie-free and accept an injected WorkOS client, so the building blocks exist; there is simply no packaging of them for Electron's runtime model.
goals: Collapse the three-context integration to one call per context — createAuthKit() in main, exposeAuthKit() in preload, <AuthKitProvider> in the renderer — replacing the roughly five hand-wired files in electron-authkit-example.

Reuse @workos/authkit-session's core (AuthKitCore, AuthOperations, sessionEncryption) for all security-sensitive logic — zero re-implemented crypto, PKCE, JWT verification, or token-refresh code — operating as a PUBLIC OAuth client: construct the WorkOS client with clientId only (no API key shipped) and inject it into the core, bypassing the API-key-requiring getWorkOS() factory and the global ConfigurationProvider.
Confine the refresh token to the main process so it appears in no renderer-facing IPC payload, while exposing the short-lived access token through getAccessToken().

Persist the session at rest via safeStorage (OS keychain), and seal the in-flight PKCE verifier with a per-install, >=32-char cookiePassword generated on first run and stored in the keychain — no static secret ships in the binary (an upgrade over the example's hardcoded key).
Own the IPC contract inside the package so consumers never redeclare channel names, and surface @workos-inc/node's User and claims types directly to eliminate type drift.
Support both sign-in ceremonies — system-browser (default) and in-app window — and the full cross-platform deep-link capture matrix out of the box.
Ship as a single ESM package with subpath exports (root for main, /preload, /react) that version in lockstep, plus an in-repo example app that consumes it.

mvp.item: Public-client config: createAuthKit({ clientId, redirectUri, cookiePassword }) constructs createWorkOS({ clientId }) (no API key) and injects it into authkit-session's AuthKitCore/AuthOperations
mvp.reason: Desktop apps are public OAuth clients; shipping a WorkOS API key in a distributed binary would leak a confidential server credential. Bypasses the core's API-key-requiring getWorkOS() factory.

mvp.item: Main-process session manager on the injected core: getUser/getAccessToken/refresh (validateAndRefresh) + cleanup(), with multi-window broadcast of auth changes
mvp.reason: The core 'server' half — nothing works without it; reuses the core's refresh dedup + rate-limit retry

mvp.item: Cross-platform deep-link capture: registerProtocol() + the open-url / second-instance / dev-argv matrix
mvp.reason: The most error-prone hand-wired piece and the backbone of callback capture

mvp.item: system-browser ceremony mode (default): createAuthorization -> persist sealedState main-side -> shell.openExternal; callback re-orchestrated outside AuthService (verifyCallbackState -> authenticateWithCode)
mvp.reason: Most secure, the recommended default; required for a usable MVP. AuthService.handleCallback is cookie-bound and cannot be reused.

mvp.item: preload exposeAuthKit() bridge with SDK-owned channel names
mvp.reason: Removes the channel-duplication footgun between preload and main

mvp.item: safeStorage-backed session persistence (refresh token confined to main) + per-install >=32-char cookiePassword in the keychain for sealing the in-flight PKCE verifier
mvp.reason: Secure-by-default at-rest storage with no static secret shipped in the binary

full.item: window ceremony mode (in-app BrowserWindow) with navigation-intercept callback capture
full.reason: Second sign-in mode for apps that prefer staying in-app

phases.title: Core session engine
phases.notes: Public-client setup: construct the WorkOS client via createWorkOS({ clientId }) (no API key) and build an AuthKitConfig object directly (clientId, redirectUri, cookiePassword; apiKey set to '' since the injected client is what is used), bypassing authkit-session's getWorkOS() and ConfigurationProvider. Integrate AuthKitCore + AuthOperations + sessionEncryption; session manager (getUser/getAccessToken/refresh/signOut/switchToOrganization); safeStorage persistence; per-install keychain cookiePassword. Pin @workos-inc/node peer to a range matching authkit-session (^10.x, aligned with the newest sibling tanstack-start; the example must bump off 8.0.0-rc.10). Unit-tested against a mocked WorkOS client; no Electron windows yet.

phases.title: Ceremony, deep-link & IPC
phases.notes: system-browser sign-in via AuthOperations.createAuthorization (returns { url, sealedState }; the auth URL carries state=sealedState). RE-ORCHESTRATE the callback outside AuthService (AuthService.handleCallback is cookie/SessionStorage-bound and unusable): persist the sealedState verifier main-side in electron-store (not a cookie), then at callback feed the deep-link state param to AuthKitCore.verifyCallbackState as cookieValue, unseal, call client.userManagement.authenticateWithCode({ code, clientId, codeVerifier }), build the Session, persist via safeStorage, and single-use-delete the verifier. Cross-platform deep-link capture (registerProtocol + open-url/second-instance/argv). IPC handlers with discriminated-union results + multi-window broadcast; preload exposeAuthKit bridge.

phases.title: React bindings
phases.notes: @workos/authkit-electron/react: AuthKitProvider, useAuth, useAccessToken, <SignedIn>/<SignedOut>. Consumes the SDK-owned IPC bridge; the renderer never sees the refresh token. Surfaces @workos-inc/node User/claims types.

phases.title: In-app window ceremony mode
phases.notes: ceremony.mode 'window': child BrowserWindow to the hosted AuthKit page, navigation-intercept callback capture, preventDefault before the protocol handler fires to avoid a double-handle. Reuses the Phase 2 callback re-orchestration.

phases.title: Example app + automated e2e
phases.notes: Seed example/ from electron-authkit-example consuming the published SDK API (resolving the package from built dist); Playwright + Electron e2e with a passing sign-in test for EACH ceremony mode; wire lint/format/export-resolution into CI.

execution.agentTeamPrompt: Phase 3 (React bindings) and Phase 4 (In-app window ceremony mode) are independent and can run in parallel once Phase 2 (Ceremony, deep-link & IPC) is complete - both depend only on Phase 2. Spawn one teammate per phase: teammate A runs docs/ideation/authkit-electron/spec-phase-3.md (touches src/react/* and src/shared), teammate B runs docs/ideation/authkit-electron/spec-phase-4.md (touches src/main/ceremony/* and src/main/deep-link.ts). Coordinate on shared files (package.json) - only one teammate edits it at a time. Each must pass `pnpm vitest run --coverage` before converging on Phase 5 (Example app + automated e2e).
